name: Question 4
problem:
Consider a curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s.$ Find the radius of curvature of $r(s)$ at an arbitrary point knowing that its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\sqrt{3}⟩.
$$
worked_solution:
Since the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are both parametrized by arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{κ(s)}=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}
$$

We differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and calculate its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s}}{2\sqrt{s}},\,\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s}}{2\sqrt{s}},\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s},\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(s)‖ & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}\cdot \sqrt{{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s})}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}\cdot \sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡\sqrt{s}+{cos}^{2}⁡\sqrt{s}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature is

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}})}=4\sqrt{s}.
$$

Question 4

Consider a curve r(s) parametrized by its arc length s. Find the radius of curvature of r(s) at an arbitrary point knowing that its unit tangent vector T(s) is given by T(s)=12⟨cos⁡s,sin⁡s,3⟩.

2s
b
4s

4s2

2s

s2

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since the curve r(s) and its unit tangent vector T(s) are both parametrized by arc length s, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature: R(s)=1κ(s)=1‖T′(s)‖

We differentiate T(s) with respect to s and calculate its magnitude: T′(s)=12⟨dds(cos⁡s),dds(sin⁡s),dds(3)⟩=12⟨−sin⁡s2s,cos⁡s2s,0⟩=14s⟨−sin⁡s,cos⁡s,0⟩‖T′(s)‖=14s⋅(−sin⁡s)2+(cos⁡s)2+(0)2=14s⋅sin2⁡s+cos2⁡s=14s⋅1=14s

Therefore, the radius of curvature is R(s)=1‖T′(s)‖=1(14s)=4s.
